messages:
Ops Bot: Alert: elevated 502/timeout rate on runtime-pool-8 (streaming paths). Threshold breached at 1914001234. Paging on-call: @riley.

Riley Gomez: ack. jumping in. quick glance at dashboards -> huge spike in stream open connections and long tail token amplification.

Riley Gomez: logs showing backpressure + queue saturation:
```
WARN 2026-03-15T15:20:10Z runtime-pool-8: apply_backpressure current_inflight=420 max_inflight=300
ERROR 2026-03-15T15:20:12Z stream-handler: write failed: broken pipe
WARN 2026-03-15T15:20:14Z runtime: shedding triggered oversized_request tokens=7892
```

Priya Singh: any recent model swaps or kernel changes on pool-8?

Riley Gomez: not that I see. last deploy 40m ago, unrelated. Looks like a few customers started large streaming jobs with >5k tokens churn and persistent connections — KV cache thrash.

Carlos Mendes: infra reports autoscale lag due to long-lived connections keeping slots occupied. We should act quickly to protect the control plane. Suggested mitigations: 1) disable streaming on generation endpoints for pool-8 2) lower max_in_flight 3) apply per-client stream concurrency limits & emergency quotas.

Riley Gomez: agreed. I'm initiating live mitigations in order that minimizes customer-impact while restoring SLOs.

Riley Gomez: Step 1 — temporary toggle: disable streaming on /v1/generation-stream for pool-8. Will fall back to non-stream chunked responses.
```
# feature toggle
PUT /controlplane/pools/pool-8/feature_flags
Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN
{"generation_streaming_enabled": false}
```

Deploy Bot: Feature flag change committed by riley at 1914001280.

Support Bot: Auto-notice sent to customers with active streaming sessions in prod-west.

Priya Singh: Step 2 — apply per-route concurrency cap and reduce max_in_flight: set max_in_flight=100, route.concurrency.generation=50. Apply gradual step to avoid client reconnect storms.

Riley Gomez: applying config change with 60s rolling window.
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/pools/pool-8/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"max_in_flight":100, "route_concurrency":{"generation":50}}'
```

Ops Bot: Config change recorded: max_in_flight=100 at 1914001315.

Carlos Mendes: Step 3 — enable adaptive shedding for oversized requests (tokens>2048) and reduce request timeout from 60s -> 25s for affected pool to avoid holding slots.

Riley Gomez: pushing shedding rules now.
```
# shedding policy
runtime.pool.pool-8.shedding={"token_threshold":2048, "strategy":"prioritize_critical_then_reject", "notify":true}
runtime.pool.pool-8.request_timeout=25s
```

Priya Singh: Step 4 — emergency per-client rate caps for noisy tenants. Creating quota overrides: c-4455 -> 10rps, c-7701 -> 8rps for 20m.

Riley Gomez: overrides in place at 1914001389. Support Bot: messages sent to client ops contacts with reason and ETA.

Priya Singh: monitoring: inbound connections stabilized, in-flight dropped from 420 -> 95 within 3m, queue depth normalizing. p95 latency improved, 502s dropping.

Carlos Mendes: good. watch for reconnect storms from clients forced off streaming — they may flood with retry loops. Consider backoff guidance in notices.

Riley Gomez: Support Bot already included recommended backoff header in notices. Also adding short-lived retry window server-side (Retry-After 10s) where we reject to help clients back off gracefully.

Priya Singh: metrics at 1914001425: error rate down to baseline+1%, stream connection churn reduced, GPU utilization decreasing.

Riley Gomez: planning staged rollback: keep per-client caps and shedding for 20m, keep max_in_flight at 100 for 30m, re-enable streaming only after 15m of stable metrics. If errors <1.5% and p95 < 1.3x baseline for 15m, start canary for streaming on a subset of nodes.

Carlos Mendes: post-incident notes: evaluate more granular streaming QoS, implement per-tenant token accounting and early-shedding path, autoscale adjustments to consider connection-based scaling vs task-based.

Riley Gomez: handoff — I need to step away at 1914001460, @priYa (Priya) can you take second-watch? I'll leave runbook notes and quick commands in incident tracker.

Priya Singh: taking over. I will monitor and execute rollback plan once stabilization window met. Escalation criteria: error_rate > 3% or reconnect rate > 200/s for 5m.

Ops Bot: Handoff recorded: Riley -> Priya at 1914001460.

Support Bot: Customers affected: flagged and notified. Ticket created for top noisy tenants; follow-ups assigned to account team.

Riley Gomez: quick checklist posted to incident board: how to toggle generation_streaming_enabled, how to push shedding policy, quota override curl snippets, rollback criteria. Also noted follow-ups: per-route QoS, dynamic stream backpressure, better client guidance for retries.

Priya Singh: will keep thread open until streaming canary succeeds. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
